{{Current events|year=2021|month=01|day=19|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Arts and culture'''
*[[List of events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic|Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
**[[Taiwan]] cancels the upcoming [[Taiwan Lantern Festival]] for the first time since 1990, amid a surge in [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases on the island. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/taiwan-cancels-major-festival-as-domestic-covid-19-cases-rise (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
*****Former presidential candidate [[Andrew Yang]], who is currently running for [[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] of [[New York City]] in the [[2021 New York City mayoral election|upcoming mayoral election]], will quarantine after one of his staffers tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/19/nyregion/andrew-yang-coronavirus.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****A memorial at the [[Lincoln Memorial]] [[Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool|Reflecting Pool]] honoring the 400,000 [[Americans]] who died from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] on the eve of the [[Inauguration of Joe Biden|inauguration]]. Additionally, 400 bells will ring at the [[Washington National Cathedral]] and a moment of silence will held. [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] and [[President-elect of the United States#Vice president-elect|Vice President-elect]] [[Kamala Harris]] will be officiating. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-usa/bells-and-candlelight-to-honor-400000-covid-19-dead-on-eve-of-u-s-presidential-handover-idUSKBN29O24X (Reuters)]
***The [[United States]] surpasses 400,000 deaths of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-19-death-toll-400k-united-states/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] extends [[work from home]] arrangements for [[civil servant]]s until January 27, as the city seeks to contain a rise in [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases that reach triple digits. [https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/hk-govt-extends-work-from-home-for-civil-servants-until-jan-27 (Reuters via ''Financial Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Shizuoka Prefecture|Shizuoka]] [[prefectures of Japan|prefectural]] government issues an emergency alert after three cases of [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]] in people with no travel history or known contact with someone from the [[United Kingdom]] were confirmed in the prefecture. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/01/998de4b50134-shizuoka-pref-issues-emergency-alert-over-new-coronavirus-variant.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****[[Kuwait]] reports their first cases of [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in two woman arriving at [[Kuwait International Airport]] who had travelled from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-reports-two-cases-of-new-covid-19-variant-1.76590091 (Gulf News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]]’s Senior Minister [[Ismail Sabri Yaakob]] announces the extension of the second [[Malaysian movement control order|movement control order]] to six states which will take effect from January 22 at 12:01 a.m. local time until February 4. It means that all [[States and federal territories of Malaysia|states and federal territories]] except [[Sarawak]] will be placed under tighter restrictions. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-covid-19-mco-all-states-except-sarawak-jan-22-feb-4-13993694 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The first 30,000 doses of the [[Pfizer]]-[[BioNTech]] vaccine arrive in [[Andorra]], sent by [[Spain]] after both governments reached an agreement this morning. [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2021/01/19/spain-plans-sell-30000-doses-covid-vaccine-andorra/ (Euro Weekly News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and the leaders of all 16 [[States of Germany]] agree to extend their nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until February 14, due to fears of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|SARS-CoV-2 new variant]]s. They also agree to mandate [[medical mask]]s for passengers on public transport. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/beschlussvorlage-corona-105.html (Taggeschau)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a new record for the second consecutive day, of 218 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,246. At the same time, the nationwide number of ICU patients reaches a record 670, just below the maximum allocation capacity of 672 ICU beds set the day before. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/323_DGS_boletim_20210119.pdf (DGS)][https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSP4N28Q028 (''Reuters'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports a record 93 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,708. [https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/arid-40210295.html (''Irish Examiner'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record 1,610 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 91,470. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-01-19/covid-uk-records-1610-more-coronavirus-deaths-the-highest-daily-figure-since-pandemic-began (ITV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***The [[New Zealand Government]] imposes a mandatory requirement for all international travellers to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test result]] before boarding an aircraft to [[New Zealand]], beginning from January 25. The requirement does not include [[Australia]], [[Antarctica]] and most Pacific Island countries. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/covid-19-coronavirus-government-extends-pre-departure-tests-to-more-travellers/HWRVBKWOXJBMTQIYQNAS62YZOU/ (NZ Herald)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Uganda–United States relations]]
**An [[Ugandan government]] spokesman accuses the [[U.S. government]] of "[[subversion]]" after [[ambassador]] [[Natalie E. Brown]] tried to visit opposition leader [[Bobi Wine]] at his home, where he is under [[house arrest]]. Brown said she wanted to check the "health and safety" of Wine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-uganda-election/uganda-accuses-u-s-of-subversion-after-envoy-tries-to-visit-wines-house-idUSKBN29O0FZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[China–United States relations]], [[Uyghur genocide]]
**The outgoing [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] declares that [[China]] has committed [[Uyghur genocide|genocide]] against [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] Muslims and other ethnic minority groups. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/china-sanctions-uighur-muslims-genocide-mike-pompeo/ (CBS News)]
  
'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[Grafton vaccine incident]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
***[[Wisconsin]] pharmacist Steven Brandenburg is charged with attempted misdemeanor property damage for deliberately trying to defrost doses of [[Moderna]]'s [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://apnews.com/article/health-milwaukee-wisconsin-coronavirus-pandemic-9443605e57f9129e11068ed80ecd2d89 (AP)]
*[[List of people granted executive clemency by Donald Trump]]
**On his last full day in office, [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] issues pardons for over 100 people. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/jan/18/trump-warned-against-self-pardon-white-house-officials-reports (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Philippine]] [[Department of National Defense (Philippines)|Department of National Defense]] terminates a 32-year-old accord with the [[University of the Philippines]], the country's [[national university]], that limits the access of [[Philippine National Police|police]] and [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|military]] personnel into the university's campuses. Faculty members, students, and activists protest the move, calling it "a violation of [[academic freedom]]" and claiming it would aid the [[Government of the Philippines|government]]'s attempts at [[Red-tagging in the Philippines|red-tagging]]. [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3118386/duterte-targets-enemies-state-university-philippines-protests (''South China Morning Post'')]
*A 65-year-old Thai woman is sentenced to 43 years in prison for [[Lèse-majesté in Thailand|insulting the Thai monarchy]] online in 2014. Her sentence, initially for 87 years' imprisonment, was reduced after she plead guilty to the charges. It is the longest punishment for ''lèse-majesté'' handed down in Thai history. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/thai-woman-sentenced-to-43-years-in-jail-for-insulting-monarchy/ar-BB1cSGJO?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters on MSN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidential transition of Joe Biden]]
**President Trump releases his farewell address hours before he is expected to leave office. Trump condemned the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]] and gave his best wishes to [[Joe Biden]] without mentioning his name. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-55727022 (BBC)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Internet regulation in Turkey]]
**[[Turkey]]'s [[Information and Communication Technologies Authority (Turkey)|Information and Communication Technologies Authority]] bans [[Advertising|advertisements]] on [[Twitter]], [[Periscope (app)|Periscope]] and [[Pinterest]] after aforementioned companies failed to appoint local representatives under a new [[social media]] law. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-twitter/turkey-slaps-ad-ban-on-twitter-under-new-social-media-law-idUSKBN29O0CT (Reuters)]
